name: 시 낭독 리허설
prompt:
Cinematic progressive ink-line animation on a solid pure bright white background (#FFFFFF), edge to edge. The very first frame is an entirely empty white field. Static locked-off camera, one continuous 8-second take.

The subjects: a master poet demonstrating expressive posture at one side of a small amphitheater stage, a performance coach guiding a nervous young poet through the same gesture, an invited guest listening from the foremost seat, a theater guard half-visible beside a velvet curtain cropped by the right edge, and a vast ascending sweep of empty seats rising behind the group.

0-3.5s: fine dark-charcoal ink strokes are traced visibly from endpoint to endpoint — each stroke confident, drawn once. The large landscape forms are drawn first with rich observational detail, the main subject last, in a few precise strokes. The composition is asymmetric — the main subject sits off-center. Built progressively, never fading in.

3.5-5.5s: fresh transparent watercolor fills the shapes FROM INSIDE, staying within the ink lines — deep mulberry on the stage curtain, peacock blue on the coach's jacket, warm honey gold on the wooden stage and empty seats, and soft jade on the guest's scarf. Every color is bright yet softened as true watercolor — no primary crayon colors. One consistent light direction from the upper right, with soft believable shadows. The white background stays pure white.

5.5-8s: the young poet lifts the chin and opens both arms into the coached pose while the master poet answers with a precise encouraging nod; a warm rehearsal light grows across the stage boards and reaches the guest's front-row seat. Everything else stays perfectly still.

Style: fine confident ink drawing with varied line weight and rich observational detail, fresh luminous watercolor, clear summer daylight, cinematic depth of foreground, middle ground and far horizon — the feel of a beautiful illustrated atlas for curious teenagers, never a kindergarten picture book. Museum-quality contemporary illustration.

Never: text, letters, primary crayon colors, muted grey or slate mood, sepia, ink-wash painting mood, fog, smiling sun, V-shaped birds, rainbows, dead-center composition, paint splatter, color outside the lines, camera movement, cuts, dissolve.
